useWhen: The user asks for a handoff, takeover note, onboarding summary or "where do I continue" document for a project they identify.
The user wants the current state of a named project, its unfinished work and the next steps written down for another person.
nearMiss: Running, building, testing or linting the project.
Fixing a failing test, finishing a refactor or otherwise changing the project.
Reviewing a pull request and approving or rejecting it.
Explaining a single function or file.
Writing or editing the project's own README.
Summarising pasted text that belongs to no selected project.

inputs.name: project
inputs.description: The local project to hand off: a directory path, or a single project the conversation already identifies without contradiction.

inputs.name: audience
inputs.description: Who reads the handoff: a new maintainer, a reviewer or an on-call engineer.

inputs.name: output-location
inputs.description: Where the new handoff file is written. Without it, the document is returned in the conversation.

read: Read-only version-control state (log, status, diff) through the host tool layer and its normal approval.
write: One new handoff file outside the project tree, or one new file at a user-chosen path.
The conversation itself, when the user does not want a file.
permissions.commandPolicy: read-only inspection only: version-control log, status and diff queries plus read-only file listing, always through the host tool layer under its normal approval. No build, test, install, package, migration or write command is run, even when the project documents one.

outputs.name: project-handoff document
outputs.description: A Markdown document with purpose, entry points, documented run/test commands, current state, open threads, a next-step checklist, per-section sources and a closing not-verified list.

successEvidence: Every factual section names the file path or read-only query it rests on.
Documented run and test commands are labelled as not executed, with the file that documents each one.
Each open thread is tied to a specific marker or state: an unchecked task, a TODO or FIXME location, or a dirty working state.
The document ends with an explicit list of what was not inspected.
No secret, key or large file body appears in the document.

failureBehaviour.behaviour: Ask which project to hand off. Produce no speculative document for a guessed project.
Report the exact path and why it cannot be used, then stop. Do not scan a parent directory for a substitute project.
Say which capability is missing (file reading or read-only version-control inspection) and mark the affected sections as not inspected, or stop when nothing could be read.
Report the last completed step and the files already read, and mark the document partial. Never present it as complete.
Write a new file with a distinct name and state what changed since the previous handoff. Never overwrite the earlier document and never modify project files.
